title: Errands
eyebrow: 28 requests that cannot be made from a screen · 13 already sent
dek: Everything this archive now needs is in a building. Each of these is written up so it can be sent as it stands.
lead:
This archive has read what can be read online. What is left is held in reading rooms, registry offices and one Australian state registry, and it needs a person to ask. **Each errand below gives the exact reference, what to ask for, what it would settle, and a draft in the language the office works in.** Nothing here is speculative: every reference has been checked to exist.

**Verify each institution's current address and request form on its own website before sending.** This page carries references, not addresses — an address copied from memory is exactly the kind of thing that goes wrong.

rows.what: Pićan parish registers — baptisms and deaths, 1880s–1910s
rows.ref: MKR / MKU Pićan (Pedena), diocese of Poreč-Pula
rows.why:
To settle **Antonio's return** and to find **Marta**. The Eleven page has Antonio going back to Istria and a Marta whose parentage this archive cannot close. Pićan is the parish; the registers are not on any film this archive can reach.

**Update 14 September 2026.** Received and forwarded by DAPA, and **Jasna Vlahović asks for the same completed request form** as for Svetvinčenat — applicant's details, delivery address, and billing details including an OIB. Not submitted: personal data.
rows.ask:
A certified copy or a scan of the entries for the surname De Franceschi / Defranceschi in the baptismal and death registers of Pićan, with the years given, plus the register's shelf reference.

**Sent 14 September 2026** from David's own account (thread 1a09e084997ce730). Awaiting a reply.
rows.draft: Poštovani, molim Vas kopiju upisa za prezime **De Franceschi / Defranceschi** u matičnim knjigama rođenih i umrlih župe **Pićan** za razdoblje ____–____. Molim i signaturu knjige. Unaprijed hvala.

rows.who: Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages Victoria
rows.what: Death certificate — Zdravko Defranceski
rows.ref: Victoria, Australia · Zdravko Defranceski, b. 1921
rows.why: He is the brother whose **resettlement file** carries the Partisan seizure that the family remembers as his father's. The certificate would give his death date, his last address, his parents as stated at death, and the informant — which is often the sibling who is otherwise invisible.
rows.ask: A historical death certificate. Victoria's index is searchable online and orders are placed through the registry's own site.
rows.draft: (An online order form — no letter needed. Search the historical index first for the exact registration number.)

rows.who: Biskupijski arhiv Poreč-Pula / Ordinariate of Pola
rows.what: Marriage dispensations for Vodnjan, 1815–1884
rows.ref: Cited in the register itself: «Dispensa … dell'Ordinariato di **Pola**», with numbers — e.g. 18 Feb 1830 № 97
rows.why: The Vodnjan marriage register **cites its own paperwork by number**. Each dispensation file names the degree of kinship and the couple's common ancestor — which is the single fastest way to join the two Vodnjan lines to each other, if they join at all.
rows.ask:
Whether the dispensation files of the Ordinariate of Pola for 1815–1884 survive, and if so how they are arranged and whether they can be consulted or copied by number.

**Sent 14 September 2026** from David's own account (thread 1a09e086d2d5d827). Awaiting a reply.
rows.draft: Egregi, sto ricercando la famiglia **De Franceschi di Dignano (Vodnjan)**. Il registro dei matrimoni della parrocchia cita dispense dell'Ordinariato di Pola con numero di protocollo (per esempio n. 97 del 18 febbraio 1830). Vi sarei grato di sapere se questi fascicoli si conservano e come si possono consultare.

rows.what: HR-DARI-254, and HR-DARI-382 kut. 1
rows.ref: HR-DARI-254 · HR-DARI-382, box 1
rows.why: The Kvarner households — Rijeka, Bakar, Ledenice — are documented and **unattached to any line**. These are the fonds most likely to attach them.
rows.ask:
Access conditions and a finding aid for both fonds, and whether reproduction can be ordered remotely.

**Sent 14 September 2026** from David's own account (thread 1a09e089168a2187). Awaiting a reply.
rows.draft: Poštovani, zanimaju me fondovi **HR-DARI-254** i **HR-DARI-382, kut. 1**, u vezi s prezimenom **De Franceschi / Defranceschi** u Rijeci i Bakru. Molim obavijest o uvjetima korištenja i mogućnosti naručivanja preslika.

rows.what: Austro-Hungarian Veritas register — the ship «Aquilone»
rows.ref: Registro Veritas austro-ungarico; also the Lloyd Austriaco lists
rows.why: To fix the **port of registry** of the *Aquilone*, which the At Sea page can name but not place. A ship's registry decides which country's crew lists you then go looking for.
rows.ask: The entry for the *Aquilone* in the Austro-Hungarian Veritas register: tonnage, build, owner and port of registry, with the year of the volume consulted.
rows.draft: Gentili Signori, cerco la nave **«Aquilone»** nel Registro Veritas austro-ungarico. Mi occorrono stazza, anno e luogo di costruzione, armatore e **porto di immatricolazione**, con l'indicazione dell'annata consultata.

rows.what: «Famiglia Franceschi», Il Rammentatore zaratino, 1859, p. 30
rows.ref: Il Rammentatore zaratino, 1859, p. 30
rows.why:
This is the **footnote behind the Zadar palace** — the Ferro-Grisogono-Franceschi house on Široka ulica. This archive cites the reference but has never read the page.

**Update 14 September 2026.** Zadar has replied and **asks for their request form**, saying they will attach the original email to it. Same pattern as Pazin. Not submitted — personal data.
rows.ask: A scan of page 30 of the 1859 volume, and of the title page for the citation.
rows.draft: Gentili Signori, vi chiedo cortesemente la riproduzione di **p. 30 del «Rammentatore zaratino», annata 1859**, contenente la voce «Famiglia Franceschi», insieme al frontespizio del volume.

rows.what: Shelf list for the Camillo De Franceschi bibliography
rows.ref: Gentileo, «Bibliografia degli scritti di Camillo De Franceschi», AMSI; Camillo De Franceschi, «Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino»
rows.why: **Camillo** is the second historian of this family and this archive holds almost nothing of him — no portrait, and none of his own writing read at first hand. The bibliography is the map to the rest.
rows.ask:
Holdings and shelfmarks for the two titles, and whether either is digitised.

**Sent 14 September 2026** from David's own account (thread 1a09e08b4e206bd2). Awaiting a reply.
rows.draft: Poštovani, molim podatke o primjercima i signaturama za: Gentileo, «Bibliografia degli scritti di Camillo De Franceschi» (AMSI), te Camillo De Franceschi, «Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino». Zanima me i je li išta od toga digitalizirano.

rows.what: The Istrian bundle — four titles at once
rows.ref: Bertoša, «Pisma Carla De Franceschija Šimi Ljubiću», VHARP 13 (1968) · Jelinčić, Jadranski zbornik XI (1979–81), pp. 293–307 · Orbanić (ed.), «Visita Spirituale del 1788 in Istria» · Carlo De Franceschi, «Uspomene», Pula–Rijeka 1989
rows.why: Four references this archive cites and has not read. The **Uspomene** are Carlo's own memoirs — the one source that might say in his own words what the 1852 marriage entry only shows: that he was gravely ill and married in a hurry.
rows.ask: Availability and reproduction of the four items, in one request.
rows.draft: Poštovani, molim obavijest o dostupnosti i mogućnosti preslika za sljedeće naslove: [list]. Istražujem obitelj **De Franceschi** u Istri.

rows.what: Notarile antico, B. 2979
rows.ref: ASUd, Notarile antico, busta 2979
rows.why: The Carnian end. The 1679 headmen's list puts a **Zuane De Franceschi of Mione** working in the county of Pazin; notarial acts are where a man of that kind leaves a second trace.
rows.ask: Whether the busta is consultable and whether a targeted search for the surname can be commissioned.
rows.draft: Gentili Signori, chiedo se la **busta 2979 del fondo Notarile antico** sia consultabile e se sia possibile una ricerca mirata sul cognome **De Franceschi** (area della Carnia, fine XVII secolo).

rows.who: Matični ured Senj (registry office) / Državni arhiv u Rijeci
rows.what: Senj birth register 1926 — Hedviga Blažević, and the Senj marriage register for 1948
rows.ref: Matična knjiga rođenih Senj 1926; matična knjiga vjenčanih Senj 1948
rows.why: Two things at once. **Hedviga's date of birth exists in this archive as both 8 March 1926 and 3 August 1926** — the same digits in the wrong order, and one of them is a transposition. And **the family remembers 1948** as the year she and Ivan Defranceski «went»; a marriage entry that year would explain the memory without contradicting their son's 1951 birth at Senj.
rows.ask: A certified copy of the birth entry for **Blažević Hedviga**, born 1926 at Senj, daughter of Ljubomir Blažević and Milka née Papić; and a search of the 1948 marriage register for **Defranceski Ivan**, born 25 June 1925 at Crikvenica, with **Blažević Hedviga**.
rows.draft: Poštovani, molim Vas ovjereni izvadak iz **matične knjige rođenih za Senj, godina 1926**, za **Hedvigu Blažević**, kćer Ljubomira Blaževića i Milke rođene Papić. Molim i pretragu **matične knjige vjenčanih za Senj, godina 1948**, za **Ivana Defranceskog**, rođenog 25. lipnja 1925. u Crikvenici, i **Hedvigu Blažević**. Istraživanje je obiteljsko i nekomercijalno. Unaprijed zahvaljujem.

rows.who: Arolsen Archives (International Tracing Service), Bad Arolsen
rows.what: Any trace of Ivan Defranceski and Hedviga Blažević leaving Yugoslavia, 1948–1951
rows.ref: ITS Digital Collections; the family is already in the Pfullingen list of foreigners and the AOK sickness-fund cards · Form: arolsen-archives.org/en/archive/inquiry/ → «Go to the inquiry form». Required: first name, last name, e-mail, subject «Archive and online archive», salutation, consent tick, reCAPTCHA.
rows.why:
**SENT by David on 13 September 2026.** Awaiting reply.

Arolsen answer tracing enquiries in writing and are not quick — weeks is normal, longer is common. Nothing further is needed from this end until they reply, except one thing: **`collections.arolsen-archives.org` has been timing out for four days** while the main site answers normally. The free search of the online collections should still be run the moment it comes back, because it may answer the question without anyone at Bad Arolsen having to open a file.

---

**Still down on 13 September 2026** — `collections.arolsen-archives.org` times out at 25 seconds while the main site answers in under four. Their outage, four days running, so the free search that should come first cannot be run yet.

**This one cannot be sent from here, and the reason is not the one previously given.** The enquiry form is protected by a **reCAPTCHA** — which this archive does not attempt to get around — and carries a **declaration of consent**, which is David's to give and not an agent's. The salutation field noted earlier is real but trivial beside those two. **The draft below is ready to paste and the send is David's.**

**This is now the most valuable single request this project has open.** The family's testimony is that Ivan and Hedviga **left in 1948 to get out of the country**; a Senj hospital birth on 17 December 1951 puts them back on the coast by about March 1951. **A failed exit leaves nothing in a Croatian register.** If anything survives it is here.

The route is not a guess. The family already had a household in **Pfullingen**, in the **French occupation zone**: Ivan worked at Reutlingen from 21 October 1941 at Brunnenstraße 7; his father Anton Rudolf is on the 1947 Pfullingen list of foreigners; his brother Anton's card is stamped «Emigré Australie le 8.3.49» and Zdravko resettled to Australia in 1949. **Ivan and Hedviga were aiming at the same door a year later.**
rows.ask: A search of the ITS holdings for **1948–1951** for **DEFRANCESKI / DEFRANCESCHI, Ivan**, born 25 June 1925 at Crikvenica, and **BLAŽEVIĆ, Hedviga**, born 1926 at Senj — in the **French zone (Württemberg-Hohenzollern, Reutlingen and Pfullingen)** and in any IRO registration, screening or rejection file. Separately: **KOVAČINA, Uršula**, born about 1890; and confirmation of which **Anton Rudolf Defranceski** appears on the 1947 Pfullingen list and the 1950 mayoral certificate, since the family records him as dying in **1943**.
rows.draft: Dear Arolsen Archives, I am researching my own family and have already used your Pfullingen list of foreigners and the Allgemeine Ortskrankenkasse card for Ivan Defranceski (Brunnenstraße 7, Pfullingen, from 21 October 1941). I should be grateful for a search of the ITS holdings for the years **1948–1951** for **DEFRANCESKI / DEFRANCESCHI, Ivan**, born 25 June 1925 at Crikvenica, Croatia, and for **BLAŽEVIĆ, Hedviga**, born 1926 at Senj — including any **IRO registration, screening or rejection** file in the French zone (Reutlingen / Pfullingen). His brothers **Zdravko** and **Anton** resettled to Australia from there in 1949 (Anton's card is stamped «Emigré Australie le 8.3.49»). I am also looking for **KOVAČINA, Uršula**, born about 1890, and for clarification of the **Anton Rudolf Defranceski** named on the 1947 Pfullingen list and certified by the mayor in 1950. Non-commercial family research.

rows.who: Matični ured Crikvenica / Župni ured Crikvenica
rows.what: The death of Anton Rudolf Defranceski, said by the family to be 1943 — and the surname Car
rows.ref: Matična knjiga umrlih Crikvenica 1943; and register entries for the surname **Car**, 1930s–1950s
rows.why:
This archive holds **two facts that cannot both be true**: Anton Rudolf Defranceski, born 20 January 1890 at Klenovica house 22, is recorded as having **died in 1943** «per the family», and is also on the **Pfullingen list of foreigners in 1947** and **certified by that town's mayor in 1950**. Everything the family remembers about his widow depends on which is right.

The same request covers **Car** — the surname the family remembers as «Carr», which on this coast is far more likely to be the Croatian **Car**.
rows.ask: A search of the Crikvenica death register for **1943** for **Defranceski / Defranceschi, Anton Rudolf**, born 20 January 1890; and any entry linking the surname **Car** with **Kovačina, Uršula**, born about 1890, in the 1940s.
rows.draft: Poštovani, molim Vas pretragu **matične knjige umrlih za Crikvenicu, godina 1943.**, za **Antona Rudolfa Defranceskog**, rođenog 20. siječnja 1890. u Klenovici, kućni broj 22. Molim i svaki upis koji povezuje prezime **Car** s **Uršulom Kovačina**, rođenom oko 1890., tijekom 1940-ih. Riječ je o obiteljskom istraživanju.

rows.who: Muzej Grada Crikvenice / Novi list archive, Rijeka
rows.what: Hedviga Blažević, a singer at the Hotel Therapia, Crikvenica, 1940s
rows.ref: Hotel Therapia (1895 Nadvojvoda Josip; Therapia from c.1899; latterly Falkensteiner, now Kvarner Palace) — programmes, posters, season photographs
rows.why: The family names the venue: **Hedviga sang at the Hotel Therapia**. That is the building that made Crikvenica a health resort — opened **1895** as the *Nadvojvoda Josip*, renamed **Therapia** when a hydropathic institute was installed. She was a **Senj** woman and Ivan a **Crikvenica** man, and this is the first explanation this archive has ever had for how the two towns met. It would also give a woman recorded here only as a wife, a mother and a date of death **a profession and a workplace**.
rows.ask:
Any programme, poster, photograph or press notice naming a singer **Hedviga Blažević** at the **Hotel Therapia**, Crikvenica, between about 1944 and 1952 — including the hotel's own season programmes for those years.

**Answered 12 September 2026 by the hotel itself.** Almost nothing survives from the Therapia years — no guest books, no personnel records, no programmes — and the present owners had already searched for the same material when they took the hotel over. They do not know where it went. **The hotel is eliminated; the museum and the Novi list archive are not.**
rows.draft: Poštovani, tražim bilo kakav program, plakat, fotografiju ili novinsku vijest u kojoj se spominje pjevačica **Hedviga Blažević** u **hotelu Therapia** u Crikvenici, otprilike između 1944. i 1952. godine — uključujući i sezonske programe samoga hotela za te godine. Riječ je o obiteljskom istraživanju, nekomercijalnom. Unaprijed zahvaljujem.

rows.who: Državni arhiv u Zadru (State Archive in Zadar)
rows.what: The Governor's Office surveillance file on Valente Defranceschi, editor of «La Trappola», 1867
rows.ref: Namjesništvo / I. R. Luogotenenza della Dalmazia — **501 IX 2/2 1097**, report of 19 September 1867; related item **493 IX 2/3 63**, 1866
rows.why:
**The first police record of this surname anywhere in the archive, and the likeliest document to give a nineteenth-century Zadar De Franceschi a father.** A political surveillance report of the 1860s normally records the subject's age, birthplace, family and employment, because that is what the officer was required to write down. The published summary — Arhivski vjesnik 35–36, Zagreb 1992, p. 131 — gives only that he was a clerk in the Zadar accounting office, fled to Italy in **1859**, worked for the Italian government, returned under amnesty, and was still taking «La Perseveranza» from Milan in 1867.

**Update 14 September 2026.** Zadar has replied and **asks for their request form**, saying they will attach the original email to it. Same pattern as Pazin. Not submitted — personal data.
rows.ask:
A scan or certified copy of file 501 IX 2/2 1097 of 1867 and of 493 IX 2/3 63 of 1866, together with any further items in the Namjesništvo fond indexed under the surname De Franceschi / Defranceschi for the years 1855–1875. Also, whether any run of «La Trappola» (Zadar, from 1867) survives in the archive's or the city library's holdings.

**Sent 14 September 2026** from David's own account (thread 1a09e08deda5627e). Awaiting a reply.
rows.draft:
Poštovani,

u Arhivskom vjesniku 35–36 (Zagreb, 1992., str. 131) navodi se izvještaj Namjesništva Ministarstvu unutarnjih poslova od **19. rujna 1867.** (signatura **501 IX 2/2 1097**) o **Valenteu Defranceschiju**, uredniku šaljivog lista «La Trappola», te srodni predmet **493 IX 2/3 63** iz 1866.

Molim Vas presliku ili skeniranu kopiju tih predmeta, kao i obavijest postoje li u fondu Namjesništva / I. R. Luogotenenza della Dalmazia i drugi predmeti pod prezimenom **De Franceschi / Defranceschi** za razdoblje **1855.–1875.**

Osobito me zanimaju **dob, mjesto rođenja i obiteljski podaci** imenovanoga, koje policijski izvještaji toga razdoblja redovito bilježe.

Molim i obavijest čuva li se u Arhivu ili u gradskoj knjižnici ijedan sačuvani primjerak lista **«La Trappola»** (Zadar, od 1867.).

Riječ je o privatnom obiteljskom istraživanju. Unaprijed zahvaljujem.

S poštovanjem

rows.what: Officer personnel sheets (Grundbuchblätter) for six men of the name, 1859–1918
rows.ref: Kriegsarchiv, Personalunterlagen — **Grundbuchblätter**, arranged by regiment and year of birth
rows.why:
**This is the document that would turn nine service entries into genealogy.** The Austrian and Hungarian printed service lists give a man's year of birth, his unit and his seniority — and never his birthplace. The *Grundbuchblatt* gives **birthplace, parents, religion, marriage and next of kin**. Six men of this name served in units this archive can now name, and not one of them can currently be attached to a household.

The prize is **Julius**: born 1879, in service from 1 July 1898, k. u. k. Kriegsmarine, still on the active list in July 1918. If he is a Fiume or Bakar man, his sheet says so, and the Kvarner households acquire their first documented officer.
rows.ask:
Grundbuchblätter, or any surviving personnel file, for:
· **Defranceschi, Julius**, b. 1879, k. u. k. Kriegsmarine, service from 1/7/1898, Linienschiffsleutnant with seniority 1/1/1909.
· **Defranceschi, Theodor**, K. K. Landwehr, Fähnrich (nichtaktiv), 27th Regiment, seniority 1 January 1907.
· **Defranceschi, Alois**, k. u. k. Heer, infantry cadet/Fähnrich, listed 1916–1918.
· **Defranceschi, Eduard**, K. K. line infantry, cadet 1859, Unterleutnant 2. Classe 1863 — **and whether this is one man or two**.
· **Defranceschi, Valentin**, K. K. Kriegs-Marine, Marine-Direktion Pola, 1854–1856.
· **Peschle, Cäsar, Dr**, K. K. Landwehr medical officer, commissioned 1 August 1895, 5th and 23rd Regiments, Landsturm district Görz.
The printed citations for each are on the archive's page «The name in imperial service».

**Sent 14 September 2026** from David's own account (thread 1a09e0a6aed7b204). Awaiting a reply.
rows.draft:
Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren,

ich ersuche um Auskunft, ob im Kriegsarchiv Grundbuchblätter oder sonstige Personalunterlagen zu folgenden Offizieren des Namens **Defranceschi** vorhanden sind, und gegebenenfalls um Kopien:

· **Defranceschi, Julius**, geb. 1879, k. u. k. Kriegsmarine, im Dienst seit 1. 7. 1898, Linienschiffsleutnant mit Rang vom 1. 1. 1909, zuletzt in der Rangliste vom 27. 7. 1918.
· **Defranceschi, Theodor**, k. k. Landwehr, Fähnrich (nichtaktiv), 27. Regiment, Rang vom 1. Jänner 1907.
· **Defranceschi, Alois**, k. u. k. Heer, Infanterie, Fähnrich/Kadett, in den Ranglisten 1916–1918.
· **Defranceschi, Eduard**, k. k. Linien-Infanterie, Kadett 1859, Unterleutnant 2. Klasse 1863 — hier wäre besonders von Interesse, **ob es sich um eine oder um zwei Personen handelt**.
· **Defranceschi, Valentin**, k. k. Kriegs-Marine, Marine-Direktion Pola, 1854–1856.
· **Peschle, Cäsar, Dr.**, k. k. Landwehr, Militärarzt, ernannt 1. 8. 1895, 5. und 23. Regiment, Landsturmbezirk Görz.

Von besonderem Interesse ist in allen Fällen der **Geburtsort**, da die gedruckten Ranglisten nur das Geburtsjahr angeben. Es handelt sich um eine private familiengeschichtliche Forschung; die gedruckten Belegstellen kann ich auf Wunsch gerne übermitteln.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen

rows.what: The December 1918 correspondence naming «Dr Defranceschi», South Slav representative
rows.ref: HHStA, **Neues Politisches Archiv 397** — Staatskanzler to Dr Defranceschi, **21 December 1918**; with the related items of 20 December (Polizeidirektion Wien to the State Chancellor) and 23 December (Cerović to the State Secretary for Foreign Affairs)
rows.why: **The last entry on the imperial-service roll, and the only one on the other side of it.** Four months after Julius Defranceschi was last printed on the Emperor's active navy list, Austria's State Chancellor is writing to a *Dr Defranceschi* as the **South Slav representative**, in the dispute over the «Bosnian Registratur» — the Austro-Hungarian archives being removed to the new Yugoslavia. The published account gives him no first name.
rows.ask: Copies of the items in NPA 397 for 20–23 December 1918 naming Dr Defranceschi, and any further correspondence in that carton under the name. **What is wanted above all is his forename and his function** — whether he acted for the Zagreb National Council, for the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, or in a personal capacity; and any address or biographical note attached.
rows.draft:
Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren,

im Neuen Politischen Archiv, Karton **397**, befindet sich Korrespondenz vom **20.–23. Dezember 1918** zur Frage der sogenannten «bosnischen Registratur». Darin wird ein **«südslawischer Vertreter Dr. Defranceschi»** genannt, an den der Staatskanzler am **21. Dezember 1918** schreibt.

Ich ersuche um Kopien dieser Stücke sowie um Auskunft, ob im selben Karton weitere Schriftstücke unter diesem Namen vorliegen.

Gesucht ist vor allem sein **Vorname** und seine **Funktion** — ob er für den Zagreber Nationalrat, für das Königreich der Serben, Kroaten und Slowenen oder in privater Eigenschaft handelte — sowie jede beigefügte Adresse oder biographische Angabe.

Es handelt sich um private familiengeschichtliche Forschung.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen

rows.who: David, with a browser — ANNO's page viewer
rows.what: Read the eight Istrian and Adriatic issues where the name appears three or more times
rows.ref: anno.onb.ac.at · the issues below, by their ANNO identifiers
rows.why:
**ANNO's search runs for this archive; its page viewer does not.** The reader at data.onb.ac.at sits behind a Cloudflare check, and this archive does not answer bot checks. So the search has been done properly for the first time — all three spellings, 950 issues, 185 of them Istrian or Adriatic — and the reading cannot be.

**These eight are the ones worth a human opening.** They are the issues where the name appears three or more times in a single issue, which for a four- or eight-page paper means a story about the family rather than a passing mention in a list.

**The first is the prize.** *Journal des Österreichischen Lloyd*, 7 September 1848, published at Trieste and Vienna — **nine occurrences in four pages**. The Lloyd's journal carried shipping movements and port and quarantine notices, and **1848 is the year Ferencz Defranceschi was running the quarantine station at Martinšćica.**
rows.ask:
Open each and save the page as PDF or text; the archive will read them:
· **oll18480907** — Journal des Österreichischen Lloyd, 7 September 1848 — **9 hits**
· **igp18950116** — Il giovine Pensiero, Pula, 16 January 1895 — 8 hits
· **igp18930118** — Il giovine Pensiero, 18 January 1893 — 6 hits
· **ist18820128** — L'Istria, 28 January 1882 — 4 hits
· **fia19120518** — La Fiamma, 18 May 1912 — 3 hits
· **edp18870903** — L'Eco di Pola, 3 September 1887 — 3 hits
· **igp18890912** — Il giovine Pensiero, 12 September 1889 — 3 hits
· **igp18960111** — Il giovine Pensiero, 11 January 1896 — 3 hits
Each opens at `http://data.onb.ac.at/ANNO/<id>`. Note that *Il giovine Pensiero* clusters in **January** — 1893, 1894, 1895, 1896 — which looks like an annual notice rather than four separate stories.
rows.sent: **Done, 14 September 2026** — read in full from ANNO's Volltext view, no page images needed.

rows.who: David, with a browser — ANNO again
rows.what: The «Defranceski» issues: two First World War casualty notices, a camp newspaper, and an official edict run
rows.ref: anno.onb.ac.at · identifiers below
rows.why:
**Three of these have now been read and the errand is reduced.** ANNO's own *Volltext* view — `annoshow?text=<paper>|<date>|x` — returns a whole issue's OCR as plain text, and with the Cloudflare check cleared in a browser it needs no page images at all. The **Journal des Österreichischen Lloyd of 7 September 1848** and the **two casualty lists** are done and published.

**These carry the family's own spelling**, which no search of the Austrian press had ever used before 14 September 2026. Three groups matter.

**The casualty lists** are new ground entirely — this archive has never looked at a First World War casualty list in any form, and here is the name in two of them a week apart in the war's first December.

**The edict run** is the interesting one. *Wiener Zeitung* on 21, 24 and 29 December 1872, and the *Laibacher Zeitung* on 3, 6 and 11 March 1875, is the publication rhythm of an official legal notice, not of news. Somebody of this name was the subject of court or estate process in Carniola across a decade.

**And the Wagna camp's own newspaper** is a different record from the intake lists the archive already holds.
rows.ask:
Open each at `http://data.onb.ac.at/ANNO/<id>` and save the page:
**Casualty lists** · nvv19141221 — 21 December 1914 · nvv19141230 — 30 December 1914
**Wagna camp paper** · lag19170204 — 4 February 1917
**The edict run, Vienna** · Wiener Zeitung, 21, 24 and 29 December 1872
**The edict run, Laibach** · Vereinigte Laibacher Zeitung, 3, 6 and 11 March 1875; and 15, 24 and 28 June 1869
**Croatian Istria** · nsp19140528 — Naša Sloga, 28 May 1914 (2 hits) · nsp18951031 — 31 October 1895 · nsp19010531 — 31 May 1901
What is wanted from the edicts is simply the forename and the town; from the casualty lists, the forename, rank, regiment and home parish, which those lists print in full.

**And three more, for a different family.** Maria née **Fernasar** is the mother of our own fourth generation and her surname has never been placed. It appears in exactly three issues of the Austrian press, and two of them are casualty lists that print forename, rank, regiment and home parish:
· *Il Giornaletto di Pola*, **8 December 1914**
· *Nachrichten über Verwundete und Verletzte*, **14 December 1914**
· *Verlustliste*, **6 May 1916**
If a Fernasar of Gračišće is in either list, her family acquires a place and a generation in one line.
rows.sent: **Done, 14 September 2026** — read in full from ANNO's Volltext view, no page images needed.

rows.who: Biskupijski arhiv Poreč-Pula / Državni arhiv u Pazinu
rows.what: Whether a second copy of the Svetvinčenat marriage register survives for 1623–1762 · ANSWERED — IT DOES
rows.ref: Matične knjige vjenčanih, župa Sveti Vinčenat (Savičenta / Sanvincenti)
rows.why:
**Answered 14 September 2026 by Jasna Vlahović of the Državni arhiv u Pazinu, and the answer is yes.**

*«Državni arhiv u Pazinu ima knjigu vjenčanih 1581-1589, 1622-1623, a knjige vjenčanih 1588-1674 i 1674-1762 imamo u digitalnom obliku.»*

Pazin holds the marriage book of **1581–1589 and 1622–1623** physically, and those of **1588–1674** and **1674–1762** **already digitised**. That covers the **1628 baptism** this archive found at Svetvinčenat and the year **1679**, and marriage acts name fathers.

**Next step, and it needs David.** Copies are issued only against DAPA's request form, which must carry his name, a delivery address and billing details (*naziv uplatitelja, adresu i OIB*). Guidance: https://www.dapa.hr/postupak-izdavanja-preslika-koje-podatke-navesti/ — 15 days if the form is complete, 30 by law otherwise. **The form has not been filled in: it is personal data and it is his to give.**
rows.ask:
Two questions only. **First**, does the diocesan or state archive hold any **marriage register or duplicate for Sveti Vinčenat covering 1623–1762** — whether a parish copy, a bishop's copy, or an extract made for a visitation? **Second**, if it does, what is its signature, and can pages be ordered by year?

If the answer to the first is no, that is the answer this archive needs, and it will be published as such.
rows.draft:
Poštovani,

molim Vas obavijest čuva li se u Vašem arhivu **matična knjiga vjenčanih župe Sveti Vinčenat (Savičenta)** za razdoblje **1623.–1762.** — bilo kao župni primjerak, biskupijski prijepis ili izvadak načinjen prilikom kanonske vizitacije.

Mikrofilm koji mi je dostupan sadrži vjenčanja za 1581.–1589. i 1622.–1623., a zatim tek od 1762. godine. Upravo u toj praznini nalaze se podaci koji su mi potrebni.

Ako takva knjiga postoji, molim Vas njezinu signaturu i obavijest je li moguće naručiti preslike po godinama. Ako ne postoji, i ta je obavijest za mene vrijedna.

Riječ je o privatnom obiteljskom istraživanju. Unaprijed zahvaljujem.

S poštovanjem

rows.what: Who Pietro Defranceschi of Ragusa was, and the Persich–Defranceschi marriage of about 1850
rows.ref: Matične knjige grada Dubrovnika; and the records of the Republic to 1808
rows.why:
**Ragusa was its own republic until 1808, with its own archive, and this project has never asked it a single question.** It now has a reason to.

Four indexed records resolve into one household: **Matteo Persich**, born 1829, son of Antonio Persich and Teresa Martecchini, married **Marietta (Maria) Defranceschi**, daughter of **Pietro Defranceschi**, and their children were baptised at Dubrovnik in 1853, 1863 and 1871.

Marietta is the only Defranceschi here whose existence is certain, and she is documented entirely through her husband and her children. **Her father is a name on one flattened index row and nothing else.** Who he was, when he came, and whether he was one of a family or alone in the city, is completely unknown.
rows.ask:
Three things, in order of usefulness:
· The **marriage entry** of Matteo Persich and Marietta / Maria Defranceschi, probably between 1848 and 1853. A marriage entry names both sets of parents and usually the bride's age and birthplace.
· Any **baptism or death entry** for a **Pietro Defranceschi** at Dubrovnik in the first half of the nineteenth century.
· Whether the surname **Defranceschi / De Franceschi** appears at all in the city's registers or in the Republic's own records before 1808.
rows.draft:
Poštovani,

istražujem obitelj **Defranceschi / De Franceschi** i u indeksima sam pronašao skupinu upisa iz Dubrovnika koji se čini da pripadaju jednoj obitelji:

· **Matteo Persich**, rođen 1829., sin Antonija Persicha i Terese Martecchini;
· njegova supruga **Marietta (Maria) Defranceschi**, kći **Pietra Defranceschija**;
· djeca krštena u Dubrovniku **1853., 1863. i 1871.** (Antonio; Cattarina Teresa Vittoria Maria, 23. prosinca 1863.; Giustino Antonio Alberto Lucciano, 26. rujna 1871.).

Molim Vas pomoć oko tri pitanja:

1. Postoji li **upis vjenčanja** Mattea Persicha i Mariette / Marije Defranceschi, vjerojatno između 1848. i 1853.? Upis vjenčanja navodi roditelje oboje mladenaca te dob i mjesto rođenja nevjeste, što mi je najvažnije.
2. Nalazi li se u maticama grada **Pietro Defranceschi** — krštenje, vjenčanje ili smrt — u prvoj polovici 19. stoljeća?
3. Pojavljuje li se prezime **Defranceschi / De Franceschi** uopće u dubrovačkim maticama ili u spisima Republike prije 1808.?

Riječ je o privatnom obiteljskom istraživanju bez komercijalne svrhe. Rado ću platiti naknadu za preslike prema Vašem cjeniku.

Unaprijed zahvaljujem.

S poštovanjem,
David Defranceski

rows.what: Put the twelve pages of defranceski.com on the public record before it is switched off

rows.what: The two Horsham probate files — Zdravko 1980 and Rosa 1996
rows.ref: VPRS 28/P10 unit 148, file 874/188 · VPRS 28/P26 unit 155, file 1113076
rows.why:
**These are the only documents that can name the Australian family's children.** Zdravko Frank Defranceski died at Horsham on 22 December 1979 and Ruža «Rosa» on 30 January 1996; the headstone gives him as «beloved husband of Rosa» and stops there. A grant of probate file holds the will, and a will names who inherits. This archive has no generation after them.

**Update 14 September 2026 — the address is now known.** The Commonwealth Gazette of 16 February 1979 lists both of them at **19 Anderson Street, Horsham 3400**, granted certificates of Australian citizenship on **21 July 1978**. Give PROV that address with the request; it is also the **last documented sighting of Zdravko alive**, seventeen months before the 22 December 1979 on his headstone — which makes the **1999** in the family file and the MyHeritage tree very hard to sustain.
rows.ask: Order copies of the two files by their VPRS references. PROV supplies digital copies of probate files; both references came off Findmypast's index of the PROV collection on 14 September 2026.

rows.who: Antenati — read them, nobody needs to be asked
rows.what: The Ovaro marriage allegati — all twenty-six files · DONE · and now the Mione registers themselves
rows.ref: antenati.cultura.gov.it/search-registry/?localita=Ovaro · Archivio di Stato di Udine
rows.why:
**Finished 14 September 2026.** Twenty-six volumes, 716 images, read end to end.

**Mione (twelve files, 420 images):** one marriage — Osvaldo × Appolonia, 1808 — plus a new generation (**Matteo**, through the daughter Orsola, 1809), a **priest** of the surname in 1785, and a **godfather** in 1789. Four of the twelve turned out to be covering letters, not allegati.

**The other fourteen files (296 images):** no De Franceschi at all — but **three Istrian documents**: Cittanova and Verteneglio 1806, Capodistria 1807, San Lorenzo near Pirano 1807.

**Since then, the Mione registers themselves.** The whole **death series 1806–1815** has been read, and the **marriage tables for 1813 and 1814**. Finds: Anna de Franceschi dead at forty-four in 1815, her husband **Paolo** alive and signing in 1812, **Osvaldo** signing twice at Muina in 1814, and **«Erman de' Franceschi»** shown to be one name and not two families.

**What remains open:** *Matrimoni* 1812 and 1815 and the six *Nati* volumes — the acts these allegati support, which would date the 1809 Cramaro marriage and might name Orsola's mother Maddalena's family. And the **Pieve di Gorto baptismal books at Luincis**, which every one of these extracts was copied out of.
rows.ask:
Open them and read. A fresh browser session is needed: a long sitting on Antenati grows the cookie until the server answers «400 Bad Request — size of a request header field exceeds server limit».

**Next, in order:** the **banns** for 1806, 1808, 1809, 1810 and 1813 (fifty-five images, arks an_ua667544–667550) · **Matrimoni 1812** (an_ua667521), which should hold the Zanelli × Roder act · **Ovaro's Matrimoni 1815**, which should hold Felice Santo's marriage · and the **Nati** volumes, which are still not located.

rows.what: Danilo Klen on the Petrapilosa fief · DONE, and generously
rows.ref: Danilo Klen, «Urbar Petre Pilose iz 1425. godine», Starine 58 (1980), 85–124 · DiZbi 177355 · and «Iz prošlosti Kostela — Petre Pilose i njegovih sela», Buzetski zbornik 2 (1977), 29–50
rows.why:
**Both articles obtained on 14 September 2026.** The library confirmed that *«Urbar Petre Pilose iz 1425. godine»*, *Starine* 58 (1980), pp. 85–124, is **fully available** in their digital collection (DiZbi 177355) — and then, unasked, **identified and scanned the second Klen article** for which this archive had a title but no journal: *«Iz prošlosti Kostela — Petre Pilose i njegovih sela»*, **Buzetski zbornik, knj. 2 (1977), pp. 29–50**.

**The 1425 urbar has been read, and it closes a line rather than opening one.** The fief's villages are **Zrenj, Čepić, Šalež, Nugla, Grimalda, Crnica, Sočerga and Kodolje** — **not Šterna and not Sovinjak**, which are the two places this family is actually documented in. The surname occurs in the article only as citations of **Carlo** and **Camillo De Franceschi**, the historians, caught disagreeing with one another in print.

**Still to read: the Buzetski zbornik article**, which is about the fief's villages specifically and may reach further south.
rows.ask: Nothing further. The request was answered in full and then some, and the thanks are owed rather than the asking.

rows.who: Archivio storico della Curia arcivescovile di Udine · and the Pieve di Santa Maria di Gorto, Luincis di Ovaro
rows.what: The Gorto parish registers — baptisms 1811–1815, and everything before 1806
rows.ref: Pieve di Santa Maria di Gorto (Luincis, Ovaro), the mother church of the Val di Gorto — Mione, Muina, Agrons, Ovasta, Luint, Cella and Liariis all baptised there
rows.why:
**The civil births stop at 1810 and this archive can go no further without the church.**

Mione's Napoleonic registers run 1806 to 1815 for marriages, banns and deaths. **The Nati run four volumes and stop** — 1806, 1808, 1809, 1810. Anyone born to these households between **1811 and 1815** is in the Gorto baptismal register or nowhere.

**And 1807 is missing from every Mione series — though not from Ovaro, whose marriages run 1806 to 1815 unbroken.** It is not missing from the year: the marriage index for 1806–1810 records *«Prencis Valentina con Defranceschi Osualdo — di Mione — 6 Agosto 1807»*. **A wedding whose act is not in the archive.** Gorto would have the church record of the same marriage — and it is worth trying the Ovaro 1807 allegati (an_ua679993) first, which costs nothing.

**Before 1806 there is no civil registration at all.** Paolo the carpenter, Osvaldo *fa legname*, Francesco the tailor, Matteo the shoemaker and Felice Santo the weaver were all born before the French arrived. Their baptisms are at Gorto, and so is the generation above them — which is the generation that would meet the 1679 weavers' list.

*The family has stood in this churchyard and photographed the stones.* What has never been asked for is the register inside.
rows.ask:
Whether the pre-1806 baptismal, marriage and death registers of the Pieve di Santa Maria di Gorto survive; where they are held — the parish, the diocesan archive at Udine, or the Archivio di Stato; and whether entries for **De Franceschi / Defranceschi / de' Franceschi of Mione, Muina and Agrons** can be copied or consulted. Specifically:

**(a) baptisms 1811–1815**, to close the gap the civil registers leave · **(b) the marriage of Osvaldo Defranceschi and Valentina Prencis, 6 August 1807**, whose Mione civil volume is lost · **(c) baptisms about 1780–1795** for Paolo, Osvaldo, Francesco, Matteo and Felice Santo.
rows.draft:
Gentile Parroco / Spettabile Archivio,

sto ricostruendo una famiglia **De Franceschi** originaria di **Mione, Muina e Agrons**, nella Pieve di Santa Maria di Gorto. I registri dello stato civile napoleonico di Mione conservati presso l'Archivio di Stato di Udine coprono i nati solo fino al 1810, e manca interamente l'anno 1807.

Vorrei cortesemente sapere **se si conservano i registri parrocchiali di battesimo, matrimonio e morte della Pieve di Gorto anteriori al 1806**, dove siano conservati, e se sia possibile consultarli o richiederne copia per le seguenti ricerche:
— battesimi **1811–1815** per il cognome De Franceschi di Mione;
— il matrimonio di **Osvaldo Defranceschi e Valentina Prencis, 6 agosto 1807**;
— battesimi **circa 1780–1795** per Paolo, Osvaldo, Francesco, Matteo e Felice Santo De Franceschi.

La ringrazio sin d'ora per la cortese attenzione.

rows.who: David, with a message — any male-line DeFranceschi of the Gračišće reunion families, or of the Crikvenica and Klenovica households
rows.what: One Y-DNA test on a De Franceschi who is not descended from David's father
rows.ref: Y-DNA — FamilyTreeDNA Y-37 or better, or a 23andMe / MyHeritage kit read for its paternal haplogroup
rows.why:
**L-M27 is the single most surprising line in this archive and it currently rests on one father and one son.**

David and Ivan both return **L-M27** — on two different companies' chips — and it is a South Asian lineage that does not appear in the Croatian reference sample at all and shows up **five times in six thousand Italians**. Ivan is 99.9% European autosomally with 0.0% of anything else. **The haplogroup has no autosomal corroboration whatsoever.**

Father and son agreeing proves only that they are father and son. **It cannot distinguish between a De Franceschi male line that has carried L-M27 since before the surname existed, and a non-paternal event anywhere in the last two hundred years** — at Klenovica, at Crikvenica, at Gračišće, at Gologorica, at Mione.

**One test on a second male line settles it, and nothing else will.**
— If another documented male-line De Franceschi is **also L-M27**, the lineage is the surname's and the two lines' common ancestor carried it.
— If he is **not**, the break lies between him and David, and the registers say exactly where the two lines part.

*23andMe's DNA Relatives runs to its 1,500-match cap and contains no living match of the surname.* The father's side clusters instead on Croatian littoral surnames — Miškulin, Vrkljan, Katalinić, Prpić-forms, Serich. **There is no shortcut through the match lists; it has to be asked for.**
rows.ask:
A male De Franceschi / DeFranceschi / Defranceski who descends **father-to-son** from one of:

**(a) Antonio DeFranceschi of Gallignana (1856–1924)** — the Eleven. His sons Antonio, Giuseppe, Gioacchino, Basilio, Rotilio, Pasquale, Nicefaro and Daniele went to New York, Tuscany and Brooklyn, and the 2012 Crystal Springs reunion album names their descendants. **This is the best-documented second line and the one to ask first.**

**(b) the Crikvenica and Klenovica households** — Ivan De Franceschi's line, and the Klenovica house 22 family.

**(c) the Gologorica pedigree** — any surviving male line off the Gologorica book.

What is needed is only the **paternal haplogroup**, not a whole kit. A cousin who has already tested at 23andMe or MyHeritage can read it off his own account in a minute; nobody needs to buy anything.
rows.draft:
Hello — I'm building a documented family history of the De Franceschi line out of Istria and Carnia, and there's one question I can't answer on my own.

My father and I have both had our **paternal (Y-DNA) haplogroup** read, and we come back the same. The Y chromosome passes father to son unchanged, so **every man who descends father-to-son from the same De Franceschi ancestor should carry the same one** — and at the moment I have only my own line to go on.

If you have tested with 23andMe, MyHeritage, Ancestry or FamilyTreeDNA, would you be willing to tell me what your **paternal haplogroup** is? It is one short code — nothing about health, nothing about relatives, and I don't need access to your account.

Whatever it says, I'll tell you what it means for both our lines.

rows.what: Crikvenica births 1909–1926 — roll ZM-34J/362, topographic mark M-6957
rows.ref: HR-HDA-1448, Zbirka dopunskih mikrofilmova matičnih knjiga i popisa obitelji; R 1909–1926, Matični ured Crikvenica; digitised
rows.why:
**One roll holds the baptisms of all five of Anton Rudolf and Ursula's children** — Josip Petar 1911, Petar Vid 1913, Anka Nera 1915, Zdravko 1921 and Ivan Anton 1925 — and this archive has not one of them.

FamilySearch's Crikvenica films stop at **Rođeni 1896**, cut at the hundred-year line as it stood when they were made, so every one of those five births falls after the end of the only collection the archive can reach for free. The supplementary collection does not stop there. **This is the single most overdue book in the archive**: five baptisms, one reel, and the parents named on every one of them.

The archive already wanted two other books from the same collection — the twentieth-century **Status animarum** (ZM-34J/251, M-5976), which is a household census that would give the whole family on one page, and **marriages 1909–1947** (the same ZM-34J/362). All three should go in one request.

rows.what: Death certificate — Zdravko «Frank» Defranceski, died Horsham, 22 December 1979
rows.ref: Victorian historical death index, 1979; the index is open to 1988
rows.why:
**A Victorian death entry names the parents of the deceased.** Zdravko's would give **Anton Rudolf Defranceschi and Ursula Kovačina** in an Australian record — and that would tie the Crikvenica family and the Australian one together in a document rather than by inference. Everything joining them at present is the Arolsen file, the ship's manifest and the family's own tree.

**Ruža's 1996 death is not yet in the open index** (Victoria releases deaths at thirty years), so it has to wait until 2026–27.

*The index alone will not do it.* A search of the free index returns a name, a year and a registration number; the parents are on the certificate, which has to be bought. This is an application, not a search — and the archive could not drive the search form from either of its browsers in any case.
rows.ask: A historical death certificate for Zdravko Defranceski (also recorded as Zorafko and Zdrafko), died at Horsham, Victoria, 22 December 1979, aged 58, buried Horsham Cemetery on 27 December — giving parents' names and places of birth.

rows.what: A fresh GEDCOM export of family tree 4
rows.ref: Family site OYYV7AGVV4FMSGNWXC6TO74JQDUMOYA, tree 4 of six — «My Family Tree (Defranceski, Lerena, Taylor, Barry, Blazevic, Booyzen)»
rows.why:
**This is the cheapest single thing anybody can do for this archive.** The roster's family file is the export of **July 2018 — 8,286 people**. The live tree holds **15,643**, and a structural walk of it on 15 September found **798 individuals of the surname where name queries had found 459**, with **313 of them carrying source citations David typed in by hand** — FamilySearch arks, film numbers, archive names. None of that is in the archive.

**It cannot be crawled out.** MyHeritage blocks a POST to a local receiver and the browser tool channel truncates at about a thousand characters, which is ten people per call — eighty calls for the names alone and more for the citations. **A GEDCOM is one click and one file.**

It is also what caught the Horsham branch missing in the first place: David looked at his own tree and asked why the archive did not have his cousin's sister.
rows.ask: Export family tree 4 as GEDCOM from MyHeritage (Family tree → Export to GEDCOM) and drop the file in the repository. Tree 4 only — the other five trees on the site are unrelated lines.

rows.what: Marriage certificate — Emerico De Franceschi and Marietta Cosulich, Cardiff, 26 July 1876
rows.ref: GRO marriage index, Cardiff district, Glamorganshire, **Q3 1876, volume 11A, page 428** (indexed as «Emmerico Defrancrschi»)
rows.why:
**The first record of this name in Wales, and it married a Cosulich.** The Catholic register at St Peter's, Roath gives the two fathers — *Francisci de Franceschi* and *Josephi Francisci Cosulich* — and nothing else. **The civil certificate gives the rest**: both ages, both residences, both occupations, and the witnesses, who at a marriage between two Adriatic families in a Welsh coal port are likely to be the other men off the ships.

Cosulich is a Lussinpiccolo and Trieste shipowning house. If Emerico is a master or a mate, his occupation on this certificate joins this marriage to [the Lloyd's List work](/at-sea/) directly. **£12.50 and a fortnight**, ordered online from the GRO with the volume and page above — no personal data of David's is needed beyond a delivery address.

*Found 16 September 2026 in the [Findmypast sweep](/findmypast/).*

rows.who: National Archives and Records Administration, United States
rows.what: Naturalisation petition — Giovanni «John» De Franceschi, Chicago, 1937
rows.ref: **NARA M1285, roll 41** — Soundex Index to Naturalization Petitions, US District & Circuit Courts, Northern District of Illinois, 1840–1950
rows.why:
**A naturalisation petition names the comune.** Every American record this archive has for the Chicago household says «Italy» and stops: the 1930 census, the burial at St Joseph's River Grove in 1951, the Soundex index itself. The petition behind the index gives **the town of birth, the date and port of arrival and the ship**.

Giovanni was born in 1895 and naturalised in 1937, so he arrived somewhere in between — and if the town is in the Val Degano or the Vinodol this is not a namesake at all. **The same document exists for Antonio of Memphis**, born 1875 in Italy and arrived 1902, and is worth ordering in the same letter.

*Found 16 September 2026 in the [Findmypast sweep](/findmypast/).*
